author: Mark Atwood
text:
Resolved in collaborative session 2026-05-12: Option B \u2014 minimal engagement.

DECISION RECORD

JMAP Chat does NOT define a DID capability, companion draft, or auth integration. The core spec adds one prose acknowledgement that DID URIs are an acceptable form of ChatContact.id alongside other URI forms (e.g., user@host). Servers MUST treat the identifier as opaque regardless of form.

This is the conservative answer: the spec doesn't preclude DID-based identity but doesn't deliver portability behavior either. Deployments that want DID-based federation auth or resolution build that out-of-band; the wire contract is unchanged from the existing 'opaque identifier from the authentication layer' model.

IMPLEMENTATION

Single prose change in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md, near the identity definition (line ~140 area, the 'id / userId:' entry, or near the ChatContact description at line 322-325). Suggested wording:

  'The specific form of the identifier (e.g., user@host, a DID URI from [W3C DID-Core], or any other URI form) is not constrained by this specification; servers MUST treat it as opaque regardless of form.'

May be filed as a small follow-up task bead, but it is minor enough to fold into the next pass of identity-section edits.

Implications for future:
- If demand for actual DID interop materializes (federation auth via DID resolution, mention syntax @{did}, etc.), file a new design-decision bead and re-open the strategic question. Option B keeps that path open.
- Today's answer means JMAP Chat is mailbox-bound in practice; users wanting DID-portable identity use a separate protocol (Bluesky / AT Protocol, etc.) and bridge if needed.

Considered and rejected:
- Option A (no engagement): unnecessarily defensive; the one-sentence accommodation costs nothing
- Option C (companion draft): rejected as over-engineering for current scope; can be revisited if demand materializes
- Option D (DID-first core): rejected as draft-00 disruption; would effectively be a different protocol
